topic: Solute and solvent roles in solutions
key_concepts: A mixture is a physical combination of two or more substances not chemically bonded
Components of a mixture retain their individual properties
Mixtures can be separated by physical means such as filtration, distillation, or chromatog
Pure substances include elements and compounds with fixed composition
Air is a mixture of gases such as nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, argon, and water vapor
Water, salt, and gold are pure substances, not mixtures
A saturated solution cannot dissolve any more solute at a given temperature
Adding more solute to a saturated solution can form a supersaturated solution
The solute is the substance that is dissolved in a solvent
The solvent is the dissolving medium in a solution
In sweetened tea, sugar is the solute and water is the solvent
In a saline solution, water dissolves salt, so water is the solvent and salt is the solute
